title: Mechanically Versatile Soft Machines through Laminar Jamming
scientific_question: Can laminar jamming provide controllable stiffness, high force capacity, and shape adaptation in soft machines through pressure-dependent interlayer friction?
reason_investigated: Primary prior art cited in D1-V001; verified as direct kill candidate against generic laminar jamming novelty.
system_description: Planar stacked paper strips enclosed in vacuum-sealed thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) envelopes; evaluated under 3-point bending and cantilever bending.
material_description: HP Ultra White Multipurpose Copy Paper (thickness 0.1 mm, Young's modulus E = 3.6 GPa, Poisson's ratio v = 0.3) enclosed in heat-sealed TPU envelopes (thickness 0.08 mm).
geometry: Rectangular beam strips, width b = 25 mm, lengths L = 75-150 mm, layer count N = 10 to 25 layers (total thickness h = 1.0 to 2.5 mm).
loading_mode: Quasi-static 3-point bending and cantilever tip bending.
boundary_conditions: Simply supported (span 75 mm) and clamped-free cantilever.
control_variable: Vacuum pressure (absolute gauge pressure 0 to -90 kPa).
pressure_or_preload_definition: Hydrostatic differential vacuum pressure Delta P = P_atm - P_int.
mechanical_model: Euler-Bernoulli beam theory extended for vacuum normal pressure, Coulomb interlayer friction, and frictional slip propagation.
constitutive_assumptions: Linear elastic paper sheets under small strains; cross-sections remain plane and perpendicular to neutral axis; envelope compliance neglected in bending core.
contact_assumptions: Interlayer contact pressure is uniformly equal to applied differential vacuum pressure Delta P across all internal sheet interfaces.
friction_assumptions: Classical Coulomb friction law with constant static/kinetic friction coefficient mu = 0.35 +/- 0.03; slip occurs when shear stress tau exceeds mu * Delta P.
slip_representation: Discrete slip thresholds between adjacent sheets; identifies pre-slip (bonded-like n^2 stiffness scaling), partial slip transition, and post-slip (unbonded n scaling) regimes.
stiffness_definition: Bending stiffness EI_eff extracted from initial linear slope of force-deflection curve.
experimental_method: Instron 5566 tensile/compression testing machine fitted with a 100 N load cell; automated vacuum regulator; laser-cut specimen stacks.
model_validation_method: Direct overlay of theoretical load-deflection predictions against experimental curves and 2D frictional contact FEA in Abaqus.
calibration_parameters: Interlayer friction coefficient mu = 0.35 (fitted from sliding tests)
independent_validation_data: Tested multiple layer counts and pressures without re-tuning friction coefficient.
main_evidence: Demonstrated stiffness tuning ratio up to 60x; validated that pre-slip bending stiffness scales as N^3 (or N^2 times unjammed); confirmed force-deflection transitions from elastic to slipping regime.
page_or_section: Sections 2.1-2.4, pp. 1707136-2 to 1707136-6; Experimental Section, p. 1707136-10.
figure_or_table_pointer: Figure 2 (mechanics model and slip regimes), Figure 3 (force-deflection validation), Figure 4 (stiffness scaling with N and Delta P).
what_it_proves: Laminar jamming beams exhibit pressure-dependent variable stiffness governed by Coulomb friction.
Pre-slip bending stiffness scales with layer count cubed (or N^2 relative to unjammed).
Euler-Bernoulli beam theory with friction slip captures the qualitative transition loads.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove validity for high layer counts (N > 25); explicitly states single-crystal homogenization as open future work.
Does not quantify output-specific model-form error boundaries across a systematic (N x p_vac x kappa) domain.
Does not formulate a homogenized continuum beam governing differential equation.
limitations: Limited to low-to-moderate layer counts (N <= 25).
Assumes perfectly uniform vacuum distribution and rigid envelope.
Quasi-static only; dynamic rate effects and viscoelasticity of TPU envelope not modeled.
threat_to_D1_claims: Fatal direct kill to broad D1 claim (CLM-D1-GEN); proves variable-stiffness layer jamming beams are known prior art.
supports_D1_claims: Directly motivates P1 and D1/M1 by explicitly identifying homogenized slip modeling for high layer counts as open future work.
conceptual_overlap: HIGH: Examines identical mechanics of vacuum-jammed planar sheets under bending.
mechanistic_overlap: HIGH: Coulomb friction, interlayer shear slip, normal vacuum pressure coupling.
experimental_overlap: HIGH: Quasi-static 3-point bending under regulated vacuum pressure.
model_overlap: MODERATE: Discrete-layer beam theory, whereas D1/M1 focuses on homogenized continuum beam models.
validity_domain_overlap: PARTIAL: Tested N in [10, 25], p_vac in [0, 90 kPa]; did not map validity breakdown limits.
breakdown_assessment: Discusses slip transition as a functional operating mode rather than model failure or validity breakdown.
model_form_error_assessment: Reports model-experiment agreement but does not isolate model-form error from parameter fitting.
reference_resolution_level: 2D plane stress continuum FEA in Abaqus with frictional surface interaction pairs.
failure_mechanism_analysis: Attributes slip onset to shear stress overcoming Coulomb threshold.
impact_on_D1: Forced pivot from generic layer jamming soft robot novelty (CLM-D1-GEN) to P1/M1 validity limit formulation.

title: Layer jamming: Modeling and experimental validation
scientific_question: How do discrete interlayer slip propagation and hysteretic energy dissipation govern the non-linear bending response of vacuum layer-jamming structures?
reason_investigated: Cited in D1-V001; established that force-deflection modeling, slip onset, and hysteresis validation were already solved.
system_description: Rectangular layer-jamming specimens made of stacked Mylar and paper strips inside sealed silicone/latex pouches subjected to cyclic 3-point bending.
material_description: Polyethylene terephthalate (Mylar) sheets (thickness 0.1 mm) and Kraft paper strips; silicone elastomer encapsulation.
geometry: Specimen width 20 mm, length 120 mm, layer counts N = 4, 8, 12.
loading_mode: Quasi-static monotonic and cyclic 3-point bending (deflection amplitudes 2 to 10 mm).
mechanical_model: Analytical Euler-Bernoulli beam model with progressive discrete interlayer slip; calculates cross-sectional shear stress distribution and slip zone propagation.
constitutive_assumptions: Elastic layer deformation; Euler-Bernoulli kinematics; Coulomb friction at sheet interfaces.
contact_assumptions: Uniform contact normal stress induced by vacuum; frictionless contact with envelope.
friction_assumptions: Amontons-Coulomb friction law with experimentally identified friction coefficient mu.
slip_representation: Layer-by-layer progressive slip tracking; calculates critical slip load for each interface.
stiffness_definition: Secant and tangent bending stiffness across pre-slip, partial-slip, and gross-slip regimes.
experimental_method: Universal testing machine (MTS Criterion) with cyclic loading protocols; digital image correlation (DIC) for surface deformation.
model_validation_method: Comparison between analytical load-deflection / hysteresis predictions and experimental force-displacement loops.
calibration_parameters: Friction coefficient mu (measured via inclined plane and tribometer)
independent_validation_data: Friction coefficient measured in independent tribological test prior to beam validation.
main_evidence: Validated discrete slip propagation model against cyclic bending tests; demonstrated that hysteresis area scales with vacuum pressure and slip displacement; confirmed transition loads match analytical thresholds.
figure_or_table_pointer: Figures 3-6 (model formulation and slip zones), Figures 7-11 (experimental validation and hysteresis loops).
what_it_proves: Discrete slip propagation in layer jamming can be analytically predicted with independent friction calibration.
Quasi-static hysteresis in layer jamming is quantitatively caused by interlayer frictional work.
Stiffness degradation during bending follows interface shear capacity.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not formulate a homogenized continuum beam governing equation (remains discrete layer-by-layer).
Does not study high layer counts (N > 12).
Does not map model-form error boundaries or validity breakdown domains across (N x p_vac x kappa).
limitations: Computationally complex for large N due to layer-by-layer interface tracking.
Restricted to small layer counts (N <= 12) and simple 3-point bending.
Does not consider out-of-plane curvature, torsion, or envelope shear transfer.
threat_to_D1_claims: Falsifies any D1 claim that experimental validation of interlayer slip onset, force-deflection, or hysteresis in layer-jamming beams is novel.
supports_D1_claims: Establishes independent friction calibration protocol; proves that discrete models become intractable at high layer counts.
conceptual_overlap: HIGH: Solves friction-induced stiffness modulation and hysteresis in vacuum layer jamming.
mechanistic_overlap: HIGH: Interlayer Coulomb slip and energy dissipation.
experimental_overlap: HIGH: 3-point bending under vacuum confinement with load-deflection hysteresis.
model_overlap: MODERATE: Discrete interface beam model vs homogenized continuum model.
validity_domain_overlap: PARTIAL: N in [4, 12], p_vac in [0, 85 kPa].
breakdown_assessment: Focuses on validating model accuracy in the tested regime; does not define or test breakdown regimes.
model_form_error_assessment: Evaluates fit quality but does not formalize model-form discrepancy.
reference_resolution_level: None (analytical model directly compared to physical experiment).
failure_mechanism_analysis: Mechanistically links stiffness drop to interface shear exceedance.
impact_on_D1: Eliminated hysteresis modeling as a viable novelty avenue in D1-V001.

title: A continuum-based model for a layer jamming beam
repository_path: data/papers/verification/D1-V002/2025-A continuum-based model for a layer jamming beam.pdf
scientific_question: Can a closed-form continuum-based mechanics model capture the continuous interlayer sliding boundary and nonlinear bending behavior of layer jamming beams under infinite-layer assumptions?
reason_investigated: Preprint / primary formulation of Zhang et al. 2025 continuum model in D1-V002; triggered pivot from P1 to M1 adoption.
system_description: Beam-stack layer jamming structures (LJS) consisting of thin PVC sheets sealed in vacuum bags, under planar bending loads.
material_description: Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) sheets (thicknesses delta = 0.3, 0.5, 1.0 mm); polyethylene vacuum envelope.
geometry: Straight and curved cantilever and simply supported beams, length L = 100-150 mm, width b = 20 mm, height h = 5.0-5.1 mm, layer counts N = 5 to 17.
loading_mode: Quasi-static monotonic bending and cyclic deflection loading.
boundary_conditions: Clamped-free cantilever and simply supported on sliding rails.
pressure_or_preload_definition: External differential hydrostatic pressure P applied uniformly across layers.
mechanical_model: Euler-Bernoulli beam theory extended to continuous medium limit (delta -> 0, N -> infinity); defines full-jamming, half-jamming, and full-sliding regimes; derives quadratic closed-form approximation for sliding boundary y_s(Q); governing differential equation for angular deformation increment.
constitutive_assumptions: Isotropic linear elastic sheet material; plane sections remain plane; axial normal strains and normal interface strains neglected; continuous sliding boundary variable y_s.
contact_assumptions: Interlayer normal stress equals hydrostatic vacuum pressure P; contact pressure uniform along length.
friction_assumptions: Coulomb friction law with constant friction coefficient mu; sliding occurs when shear stress exceeds mu * P.
slip_representation: Continuous sliding boundary y_s across beam height, dividing cross-section into stuck elastic core and slipping outer layers.
stiffness_definition: Equivalent moment of inertia I_eq(y_s) bounded between solid beam limit (b*h^3/12) and unbonded liquid-like limit (b*delta^2*h/12).
experimental_method: Tensile testing machine with sliding support fixture to eliminate horizontal constraints; proportional vacuum regulation; cyclic displacement cycles (+/-3 mm).
model_validation_method: Comparison of analytical governing equation against 2D Abaqus FEA (CPS4R elements) and physical experiments.
calibration_parameters: Friction coefficient mu and Young's modulus E (fitted from single specimen response)
independent_validation_data: Parameters fitted from one specimen response rather than measured independently.
main_evidence: Derived closed-form quadratic approximation for y_s(Q); developed iterative stress-increment algorithm for large deflections; showed critical loads scale with pressure P; confirmed qualitative cyclic hysteresis.
figure_or_table_pointer: Figures 1-4 (continuum derivation and stress regimes), Figures 5-9 (FEA and experimental validation).
what_it_proves: A homogenized continuum model can represent layer jamming beam bending by treating the sliding boundary as a continuous variable y_s.
An analytical quadratic relationship between shear force Q and sliding boundary y_s can solve the implicit transcendental equilibrium equation.
The model reproduces the transition from full jamming to half jamming and full sliding.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove validity across broad parameter grids; overestimates critical load at low vacuum and thin layers.
Does not isolate model-form error from parameter calibration fitting.
Does not map the operational validity domain where continuum assumptions break down.
limitations: Fitted E and mu from experimental bending rather than independent tests.
Overestimates critical load at low hydrostatic pressure and thin layers.
Averaging discrete layer interactions into a continuous variable y_s introduces model-form discrepancy for low N.
Restricted to 2D planar bending.
threat_to_D1_claims: Fatal direct threat to P1 claim (homogenized slip model development novelty); proves that the continuum model formulation already exists.
supports_D1_claims: Serves as the precise baseline model M1 for D1; authors explicitly state discrepancy at low pressures and thin layers, leaving validity boundary quantification open.
conceptual_overlap: CRITICAL: Exactly formulates the continuum homogenized layer-jamming beam model proposed in P1.
mechanistic_overlap: CRITICAL: Continuous sliding boundary y_s, Coulomb friction, variable equivalent moment of inertia I_eq.
experimental_overlap: HIGH: PVC layer stacks under vacuum 3-point and cantilever bending.
model_overlap: CRITICAL: Exact mathematical formulation of baseline model M1.
validity_domain_overlap: HIGH: Tested N in [5, 17], P in [40, 100 kPa]; noted discrepancies.
breakdown_assessment: Acknowledges discrepancy at low pressure and thin layers as a qualitative limitation, but does not formalize a validity domain map.
model_form_error_assessment: Does not isolate model-form error from parameter calibration.
reference_resolution_level: 2D plane stress CPS4R finite element analysis in Abaqus.
failure_mechanism_analysis: Attributes discrepancy qualitatively to non-uniform vacuum pressure and fixture compliance.
impact_on_D1: Directly forced the reformulation from P1 (model development) to D1/M1 (validity limits of M1 across N x p_vac x kappa).

title: The global-local mechanical behaviors of multilayered structure and interface slip

scientific_question: How can global-local beam theories quantify permissible deformation and rotation limits in multilayered structures undergoing interlayer slip?
reason_investigated: Focal paper for C04 in D1-V007; subject of semantic correction CORR-01 regarding a priori predeclared vs post-hoc adopted error tolerances.
system_description: Multilayered laminated beam structure under transverse bending with unbonded frictional contact interfaces.

geometry: Multilayered beam, layer count N = 3 to 10, rectangular cross section.
loading_mode: Quasi-static bending under concentrated and distributed loads.
boundary_conditions: Simply supported and clamped beam boundary conditions.
control_variable: Applied transverse load and interlayer friction coefficient.

independent_validation_data: FEA discrete contact reference used as benchmark.

limitations: Post-hoc error threshold adoption introduces retrospective bias.
